entries.not_relevant_because: The family's theorem is about whether a connective p-complete spectrum of fp-type two lies in the thick subcategory generated by BP<2>; it is a finite-generation counterexample to the Hahn-Wilson conjecture, not a statement about telescopes. Its only telescope content is Proposition scope:telescopes in the section 'The counterexample and its localizations': for the one spectrum X constructed (at sufficiently large primes), L_2^f X ≃ L_2 X and L_{T(2)} X ≃ L_{K(2)} X. That is a comparison for a single object, not a claim that L_n^f → L_n is an equivalence for all spectra, all heights or all primes, and the manuscript says these comparisons 'neither assume nor settle the general restricted telescope conjecture for fp-spectra'. The unrestricted telescope conjecture is not addressed; the introduction cites Burklund-Hahn-Levy-Schlank as having already disproved it at every prime and height at least two.
